raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. Two hundred mu is a lot of ground for just me and my wife to run, so I've had to figure out what works and stick with it. Twenty-five years in, I know these fields.

## Thinking it through

**Land allocation.** The bulk of my land — about 160 mu — goes into the wheat-maize rotation. That's the main business. Twenty mu I put into cabbage because vegetables bring in more money per mu if you can handle the labor, and another 20 mu of millet on the piece of land out west where the soil is lighter and the well doesn't reach so well. Millet doesn't need much water and I don't have to baby it.

**Labor is my biggest worry.** Only two of us in the household. For 200 mu I have to run machinery for everything — I've got my own rotary tiller and planter, and I hire a combine for wheat harvest and maize harvest. For cabbage I bring in seasonal help from the village, six or seven people for transplanting and another round for harvest. Without hired labor I couldn't do the cabbage at all.

**Wheat (160 mu).** Planting around October 10-15 after the maize comes off. I use an improved variety — Jimai or whatever the seed shop has that year, about 45 yuan/mu of seed. The extension station guy said 15 kg N per mu is plenty but I usually put on a bit more, maybe 17-18, because I'm pushing for 500 kg/mu yield and I've seen what happens when you skimp. I put down compound fertilizer as base before sowing and topdress urea at jointing in March. Three irrigations — one before winter to help overwintering, one at jointing, one at grain fill. Herbicide for sure, and a fungicide spray around heading if powdery mildew shows up like it did two years ago.

**Maize (160 mu, same fields).** The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is tight — maybe five days. I no-till drill directly into the wheat stubble, mid-June. Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed, have to buy fresh each year. About 16 kg N/mu, one shot at planting as a controlled-release compound so I don't have to topdress — saves me a trip across 160 mu. One irrigation at tasseling if July is dry. Herbicide after planting, and I keep an eye out for armyworm. Yield target around 550 kg/mu, that's what I've been getting.

**Cabbage (20 mu).** This is the money crop but also the headache. I do autumn cabbage — buy seedlings from the nursery in early August, transplant, harvest in November. Cabbage eats fertilizer — I put on maybe 25 kg N/mu plus phosphorus and potassium, and I try to get some chicken manure from the poultry farm if I can. Irrigation six, seven times, it won't form heads without water. Spray for cabbage worm and aphids multiple times, can't avoid it. Yield 5500-6000 kg/mu if the weather holds.

**Millet (20 mu).** Easy crop. Plant late April, harvest late August. Traditional variety, I save my own seed. Maybe 8 kg N/mu of urea at planting, that's it. One irrigation if May is dry, otherwise rainfed. Light herbicide once. Low cost, low risk — it's what I fall back on for the lighter ground.

**Cash flow.** Total input costs run around 155,000 yuan across everything. The cabbage alone is about 30,000 of that. I keep some cash reserve because things happen — a pump breaks, a seedling batch fails, prices crash.
